unusual_experiment.name: MINIMAL_ENV_EMPTY_PATH_NO_HOME_FOREIGN_CWD
unusual_experiment.intervention: Invoke the exact downloaded EntityOS artifact from / with env -i, PATH=/nonexistent, no HOME, LC_ALL=C, and an isolated TMPDIR.
unusual_experiment.interpretation: At the tested self-test boundary the one-file candidate did not depend on HOME, PATH lookup, repository cwd, or persistent extraction residue. This is bounded portability evidence, not whole-machine acceptance.

grf_collapse.observed_reality: An exact one-file EntityOS built from current product main is available as a workflow artifact and passed the canonical self-hosted Linux X64 gate.
grf_collapse.preferred_hypothesis: The current single-file bootstrap is materially portable at its admitted self-test boundary and does not hide a basic HOME/PATH/cwd dependency.
grf_collapse.strongest_counterhypothesis: The frozen artifact only succeeds in the workflow runner environment and implicitly needs normal user environment variables or repository-relative working-directory state.
grf_collapse.discriminator: Re-run the exact artifact under an almost empty environment and foreign cwd, compare deterministic self-test output, and inspect temporary extraction cleanup.

release_blocker: Whole-machine acceptance remains false. The current canonical workspace still requires the smallest Clay-native Bytes/Buffer ownership+lifetime plus String/argv/effect-signature surface shared by CM-DATA and CM-TERM, followed by a provenance-bound canonical typed/effect IR -> single ClayVM path and rebuild/retest of EntityOS.
next_executable_action: Implement and test the smallest admitted Clay Bytes/Buffer plus String/argv/effect signature surface across checker/executable TypedIR/ClayVM, route one real process request without integer request-handle indirection or backend-local semantics, then rebuild and rerun the exact one-file EntityOS gates.
